<!-- file: Samples~/DOTweenUsage/README.md -->

# DOTween Usage

Core plus the DOTween integration: a view animated by the package's `TweenTransition`, and a view animated by a
transition of your own written on DOTween. Needs DOTween, the uGUI package (`com.unity.ugui`, which includes
TextMeshPro) and UniTask.

## Setup

1. Have DOTween in the project, in one of three ways:
   - DOTween from the Asset Store, with its setup run (`Tools > Demigiant > DOTween Utility Panel > Setup DOTween`);
     that defines `DOTWEEN`.
   - A UPM DOTween package: the package detects it through a version define, nothing to do.
   - Neither define is set but the DOTween assembly is in the project: turn the integration on by hand with
     `Tools/UIDirector/DOTween Integration`.
   The sample's assembly compiles only when one of these is active.
2. Import TextMeshPro's Essential Resources once: `Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources`.
   The texts stay blank until then.
3. Open the scene `DOTweenUsage.unity` from the folder the Package Manager imported the sample into:
   `Assets/Samples/UIDirector/<version>/DOTween Usage/`. The scene has no Event System on purpose: the right input
   module depends on your project's input handling, so the bootstrap creates one when Play starts.
4. Press Play. Optionally open `Window > UIDirector` to watch the stacks and the shield live (it shows something
   in Play Mode only).

The view ids in this sample (`welcome`, `hint`, `card`) differ from the ids in the other samples, so importing
several samples into one project never makes `Tools/UIDirector/Validate Catalogs` report a duplicate.

## What to do

The catalog has three rows: `welcome` (a screen that keeps its instance, with the core `FadeTransition`), `hint` (a
popup that closes on a tap on the backdrop) and `card` (a popup). The scene's root has "Initialize On Awake" off;
the bootstrap initialises it in `Awake`. The sample writes nothing to the Console: what you check is the motion.

- **Play** opens the welcome screen on its own (`source=boot`), with a fade. It has two buttons, "Show hint" and
  "Show card".
- **Show hint** opens the hint popup (`source=welcome.hint`) with the text "TweenTransition fades and scales this
  popup." and an "OK" button. It fades in while scaling up from the hidden scale (0.85 by default) and leaves the same way in reverse. This is
  the package's `TweenTransition`, set up only in the Inspector of the `Hint` prefab, with no code. "OK" or a tap
  on the backdrop closes it.
- **Show card** opens the card popup (`source=welcome.card`) with the text "PunchTransition is a custom transition
  built on DOTween." and an "OK" button. It fades in with a short scale punch (a quick overshoot that settles back)
  and leaves by fading out while shrinking to 0.9. This is the sample's own `PunchTransition`. "OK" closes it; the
  card does not close on the backdrop.
- **Pause the game while a popup opens** (`Time.timeScale` set to 0): both popups still animate, because both transitions run on unscaled time.

## What to look at

- The `Hint` prefab: select the root of the prefab and read the `TweenTransition` component. Fade, scale, offset,
  duration and the two eases are fields. The `Card` prefab uses the same view class, [HintView](HintView.cs), with
  `PunchTransition` instead; only the transition differs.
- What `TweenTransition` does: it fades a `CanvasGroup` (added when missing), scales the view from a hidden scale
  to 1 and can move it by a fraction of its layer, all with DOTween on unscaled time. It sets the ease, the auto
  kill and the update mode on the sequence itself, so project-wide DOTween defaults (a changed default ease or
  auto-kill off) cannot change the result or make the wait for the end stall.
- What `PunchTransition` shows: how to write your own transition on DOTween. Read [PunchTransition](PunchTransition.cs)
  for the pieces: it derives from `ViewTransition`, it plays a sequence with an explicit ease, auto-kill and
  unscaled time, it creates its getter and setter once, and its `Snap` never throws. It waits for the sequence by
  polling on the player loop instead of resuming from a kill callback, so a kill from `OnDestroy` never resumes the
  caller inside Unity's destroy message.
- `Window > UIDirector`: the welcome screen in `screens`; the hint or the card in `popups` while it is open.
- The Hierarchy: the root made with `GameObject > UI > UIDirector Root` has "Initialize On Awake" off; the
  `Bootstrap` object holds `DOTweenBootstrap`. The prefabs are in `Prefabs/`: Welcome, Hint and Card.
- [DOTweenBootstrap](DOTweenBootstrap.cs) - the root initialised in `Awake`, the welcome screen opened in `Start`
  with the root as the owner.
- [WelcomeView](WelcomeView.cs) - two buttons that open popups with the root as the owner.
- [HintView](HintView.cs) - a popup with a text and an "OK" button, shared by the hint and the card.
- [TweenViews](TweenViews.cs) - the three keys and the argument struct.
- [PunchTransition](PunchTransition.cs) - the custom transition.
- [SampleEventSystem](Support/SampleEventSystem.cs) - the event system creation.

---

<!-- file: Samples~/QueueUsage/README.md -->

# Queue Usage

Core only: no DOTween, no Zenject. Needs the uGUI package (`com.unity.ugui`, which includes TextMeshPro) and
UniTask.

## Setup

1. Import TextMeshPro's Essential Resources once: `Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources`.
   The texts stay blank until then.
2. Open the scene `QueueUsage.unity` from the folder the Package Manager imported the sample into:
   `Assets/Samples/UIDirector/<version>/Queue Usage/`. The scene has no Event System on purpose: the right input
   module depends on your project's input handling, so the bootstrap creates one when Play starts.
3. Press Play. Optionally open `Window > UIDirector` to watch the queue and the input shield live (it shows
   something in Play Mode only). Click the Game view once so it has keyboard focus: device back is the Escape key
   in the editor.

The view ids in this sample (`lobby`, `notice`, `ask`, `tutorial-tip`, `news`) differ from the ids in the Basic
Usage sample, so importing both samples into one project never makes `Tools/UIDirector/Validate Catalogs` report a
duplicate.

## What to do

Console lines come from two [QueueEventLog](QueueEventLog.cs) instances: `[queue] ...` for what the queue itself
reports (`Enqueued` when it accepts an item, `NotShown` when it turns one away or drops it), and `[views] ...` for
everything the navigator reports once an item is presented (`Requested`, `Shown`, `Closed`, `NotShown`, `Settled`).
Every line has the request id, the view id, the priority and the source tag.

- **Play**, without pressing anything: the lobby opens (`Requested ... lobby priority=0 source=boot`) and the
  bootstrap queues the startup notices at the same moment. The Console shows `[queue] Enqueued ... source=startup.news`
  with `priority=10` first and `[queue] Enqueued ... source=startup.maintenance` with `priority=100` second. Once the
  lobby is shown, the queue presents "Maintenance" first, although it was queued second, because the higher
  priority goes first. Close it with "OK" (`Closed ... reason=Dismissed`) and "What is new" follows at once. Only one
  popup is on screen at a time. The lobby status reads "Pick an action." and its buttons answer after the notices
  are gone.
- **Show startup notices** queues the same two notices again. The status reads "Notices queued. They appear one
  at a time, most urgent first." and the order is the same: "Maintenance" (priority 100), then "What is new"
  (priority 10). With `Window > UIDirector` open, the `startup` queue shows `Presenting:` the first notice and
  `Waiting (1)` for the second while the first is open.
- **Ask for feedback** sets the status "Waiting for the question to reach the screen..." and queues a yes or no
  question with the lowest priority (`priority=1`, `source=startup.feedback`). With nothing else waiting it
  appears at once: "Would you like to tell us what to improve?" with "Yes" and "No". "Yes" sets the status to
  "Thanks!". "No" sets "Maybe later.", and so does closing the popup with Escape, because a close without an
  answer carries no value.
- **Run the tutorial** sets the status "Tutorial started. Queued notices wait until it ends.", takes a hold on the
  `startup` queue named `tutorial`, and opens three tips one after the other (`source=tutorial`): "Step 1 of 3",
  "Step 2 of 3", "Step 3 of 3". Each tip's "Next" button closes it and the next one opens right away. The tips are
  shown directly, so the hold does not affect them. In `Window > UIDirector` the `startup` queue reads `held` and
  lists one hold. When the third tip closes, the hold is removed and the queue carries on; the lobby status keeps
  its text. Escape on a tip leaves the tutorial early: the tip closes with `reason=Back`, the remaining tips are
  not shown and the hold is removed in the same moment.
- **What the gate does during the tutorial**: while the tutorial runs, [OnboardingGate](OnboardingGate.cs) turns away
  every queued request below priority 100, and lets 100 and above wait for the hold. A turned-away request never
  enters the queue: the Console shows no `Enqueued` line, only
  `[queue] NotShown #n notice priority=10 source=startup.news rejected=Denied detail=onboarding is running`.
  A tip is a modal popup that covers the lobby, so you cannot press a lobby button while the tutorial runs. The
  line appears when code queues something meanwhile, which is what the gate and the hold are written for.
- **Add news feature** adds `NewsCatalog.asset` to the running navigator (the root's own catalog list holds only
  `QueueUsageCatalog.asset`) and queues one popup from it: `[queue] Enqueued ... news priority=50 source=news.added`.
  The popup appears right away: title "News", text "A news feature was added at run time.", and an "OK" button.
  The button's label becomes "Remove news feature". The popup and the catalog share one owner.
- **Remove news feature** ends that owner: the catalog is taken off the root and the label becomes "Add news
  feature" again. If the news popup were still waiting in the queue it would end as
  `NotShown ... rejected=OwnerEnded`, and if it were open it would close with `reason=OwnerEnded`. By hand the
  popup is already closed when you reach the button, because an open popup covers the lobby, so you see only the
  catalog leaving and the label changing. Press "Add news feature" again and a new catalog registration and a
  new news popup follow.
- **Escape** closes the popup on top with `reason=Back` (a notice, the question or a tip). With only the lobby
  on screen it does nothing: the lobby is the root of the history and the sample wires no quit.

## What to look at

- The Console. A notice that was queued second but has the higher priority is presented first: compare the
  `Enqueued` order with the `Requested` order. A denied request is the only kind that shows `NotShown` without a
  preceding `Enqueued`.
- `Window > UIDirector`: the `Queue startup (layer popups)` section with `Held`, `Gates: 1`, `Holds`,
  `Presenting` and `Waiting`, and the `Events` list that mixes `[queue]` and navigator events.
- The Hierarchy: the root made with `GameObject > UI > UIDirector Root` has "Initialize On Awake" off and carries
  `BackInput`. The `Bootstrap` object holds `QueueBootstrap`, whose `News Catalog` field points at
  `NewsCatalog.asset`; that catalog is not on the root. The prefabs are in `Prefabs/` (Lobby, Notice, News, Ask,
  TutorialTip) and `QueueUsageCatalog.asset` lists the ones the root owns.
- [QueueBootstrap](QueueBootstrap.cs) - the setup: the root initialised in `Awake`, the services built in
  `Start`, one log registered on the navigator and on the queue, the lobby opened, the startup notices queued.
- [StartupNotices](StartupNotices.cs) - the queue on the popups layer, a gate with the root's lifetime, the two
  priorities, and `EnqueueAsync` for the question, whose answer is read through `HasValue` because the call also
  completes when the item is turned away.
- [OnboardingGate](OnboardingGate.cs) - a gate asked at enqueue and again right before presentation.
- [TutorialFlow](TutorialFlow.cs) - a flow that takes a `Hold` and shows its own tips directly, with the hold
  removed in a `finally` so no way out of the flow leaves the queue held.
- [NewsFeature](NewsFeature.cs) with [NewsViews](NewsViews.cs) - a feature that brings its own keys and catalog,
  adds the catalog with an owner, and ends everything by ending that owner.
- [LobbyView](LobbyView.cs), [NoticeView](NoticeView.cs), [AskView](AskView.cs), [TutorialTipView](TutorialTipView.cs)
  and [QueueViews](QueueViews.cs) - the views and the keys.
- [QueueEventLog](QueueEventLog.cs) - one observer registered twice, because an item's events come from two
  publishers: the queue (`Enqueued` and its own `NotShown`) and the navigator.
- [QueueServices](QueueServices.cs), [OnboardingState](Support/OnboardingState.cs) and
  [SampleEventSystem](Support/SampleEventSystem.cs) - what the lobby's buttons drive, the flag the tutorial sets
  and the gate reads, and the event system creation.

---

<!-- file: Samples~/ZenjectUsage/README.md -->

# Zenject Usage

Core plus the Zenject integration: the container creates the services and injects them into every view. Needs
Zenject or Extenject, the uGUI package (`com.unity.ugui`, which includes TextMeshPro) and UniTask.

## Setup

1. Have Zenject or Extenject installed and the integration active. With Zenject under `Assets`, turn it on with
   `Tools/UIDirector/Zenject Integration`. With Extenject 9.0.0 or newer from UPM it turns on by itself. The
   sample's assembly compiles only when the integration is active.
2. Import TextMeshPro's Essential Resources once: `Window > TextMeshPro > Import TMP Essential Resources`.
   The texts stay blank until then.
3. Open the scene `ZenjectUsage.unity` from the folder the Package Manager imported the sample into:
   `Assets/Samples/UIDirector/<version>/Zenject Usage/`. The scene has no Event System on purpose: the right input
   module depends on your project's input handling, so the sample creates one when Play starts.
4. Add the Scene Context yourself: choose `GameObject > Zenject > Scene Context`, then drag the `AppInstaller`
   component of the `Installers` object into the Scene Context's Mono Installers list. The scene ships no Scene
   Context, because Zenject's script GUIDs depend on how Zenject was installed.
5. Press Play. Optionally open `Window > UIDirector` to watch the stacks and the shield live (it shows something
   in Play Mode only).

The view ids in this sample (`scoreboard`, `reset-score`) differ from the ids in the other samples, so importing
several samples into one project never makes `Tools/UIDirector/Validate Catalogs` report a duplicate.

## What to do

The catalog has two rows: `scoreboard` (a screen that keeps its instance) and `reset-score` (a popup that closes on
a tap on the backdrop). The sample writes nothing to the Console: what you check is the score on screen.

- **Play** opens the scoreboard on its own (`source=boot`), from `AppStart`, which the container runs once it is
  built. The score label reads "0". The buttons are "Add point" and "Reset score".
- **Add point** adds one to the score and the label shows the new number. The score lives in `ScoreService`, a
  single instance bound by the installer, not in the view.
- **Reset score** opens the reset popup (`source=scoreboard.reset`) with the question "Reset the score of N?",
  where N is the current score, and the buttons "No" and "Yes". "Yes" closes it with a true answer: the score goes
  to 0 and the label reads "0". "No" closes it with a false answer and nothing changes. A tap on the backdrop, and
  closing it any other way, end without a value and also change nothing.
- **Reset score with a score of 0** still opens the popup and asks "Reset the score of 0?".

## What to look at

- What the installer does: [AppInstaller](AppInstaller.cs) binds `ScoreService`, calls `NavigatorInstaller.Install`
  and binds `AppStart`. `NavigatorInstaller` initialises the root with the container as its injector, so the root's
  "Initialize On Awake" must be off: if the root was initialised already, `Install` throws an
  `InvalidOperationException` that names the root.
- When injection happens: every new view instance is injected while it is still inactive, before its `Awake`.
  [ScoreboardView](ScoreboardView.cs) and [ResetScoreView](ResetScoreView.cs) receive `ScoreService` in a method
  marked `[Inject]`, so the service is there in `OnOpen`. The scoreboard is a kept instance: it is injected once,
  and not again when it opens a second time (the screen reads the score again in `OnVisible` instead). The reset
  popup is not kept, so every open creates and injects a new instance.
- The root's scope: the container that injects the views is the one the root was installed into. A root under an
  app-wide context cannot see bindings that live in a scene's context. Use a scene-owned root, as this sample
  does, or pass the data as arguments of the open call.
- `Window > UIDirector`: the scoreboard in `screens`; the reset popup in `popups` while it is open.
- The Hierarchy: the root made with `GameObject > UI > UIDirector Root` has "Initialize On Awake" off; the
  `Installers` object holds `AppInstaller` with its root field wired. The prefabs are in `Prefabs/`: Scoreboard and
  ResetScore.
- [AppInstaller](AppInstaller.cs) - also creates the event system, before the root initialises and never while
  the container is validating.
- [AppStart](AppStart.cs) - opens the scoreboard once the container is built, with the root as the owner.
- [ScoreboardView](ScoreboardView.cs) - a screen with an injected service, and a popup awaited with `ShowAsync`
  whose answer is read through `HasValue`.
- [ResetScoreView](ResetScoreView.cs) - a confirm popup that completes with true or false.
- [ZenjectViews](ZenjectViews.cs) - the two keys.
- [ScoreService](Support/ScoreService.cs) - the stand-in for your own game state.
- [SampleEventSystem](Support/SampleEventSystem.cs) - the event system creation.

<!-- file: Samples~/AddressablesUsage/Support/SampleEventSystem.cs -->

```csharp
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.EventSystems;
#if UIDIRECTOR_SAMPLES_INPUT_SYSTEM && ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM
using UnityEngine.InputSystem.UI;
#endif

namespace Ecanakli.UIDirector.Samples.AddressablesUsage
{
    /// <summary>Creates the EventSystem at start; the scene ships none because a baked input module is a missing script, or throws, in projects with the other input handling.</summary>
    public static class SampleEventSystem
    {
        public static void EnsureExists()
        {
            if (Object.FindAnyObjectByType<EventSystem>() != null)
                return;

            var eventSystem = new GameObject("EventSystem", typeof(EventSystem));
#if UIDIRECTOR_SAMPLES_INPUT_SYSTEM && ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM
            eventSystem.AddComponent<InputSystemUIInputModule>();
#else
            eventSystem.AddComponent<StandaloneInputModule>();
#endif
        }
    }
}
```

<!-- file: Samples~/BasicUsage/Support/ItemLibrary.cs -->

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Ecanakli.UIDirector.Samples.BasicUsage
{
    /// <summary>Stand-in item list with three items, one of which cannot be renamed.</summary>
    public sealed class ItemLibrary : IItemLibrary
    {
        private const string ArchiveId = "archive";

        private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _titles = new Dictionary<string, string>
        {
            { "guide", "Getting started" },
            { "notes", "Release notes" },
            { ArchiveId, "Archive" }
        };

        public event Action<string> Renamed;

        public int Count
        {
            get { return _titles.Count; }
        }

        public string GetTitle(string itemId)
        {
            return _titles.TryGetValue(itemId, out var title) ? title : itemId;
        }

        public bool CanRename(string itemId)
        {
            return itemId != ArchiveId && _titles.ContainsKey(itemId);
        }

        public void Rename(string itemId, string title)
        {
            if (!CanRename(itemId))
                return;

            _titles[itemId] = title;
            Renamed?.Invoke(itemId);
        }
    }
}
```

<!-- file: Samples~/BasicUsage/Support/LegacyPopup.cs -->

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

namespace Ecanakli.UIDirector.Samples.BasicUsage
{
    /// <summary>Stand-in for a popup from an older UI system that the package does not run.</summary>
    public sealed class LegacyPopup : MonoBehaviour
    {
        public bool IsOpen
        {
            get { return gameObject.activeSelf; }
        }

        public void Show()
        {
            gameObject.SetActive(true);
        }

        public bool TryClose()
        {
            if (!IsOpen)
                return false;

            gameObject.SetActive(false);
            return true;
        }
    }
}
```

<!-- file: Samples~/BasicUsage/Support/SettingsStore.cs -->

```csharp
using System;
using System.Threading;
using Cysharp.Threading.Tasks;
using UnityEngine;

namespace Ecanakli.UIDirector.Samples.BasicUsage
{
    /// <summary>Stand-in settings storage that only logs and waits.</summary>
    public sealed class SettingsStore : ISettingsStore
    {
        public void ResetToDefaults()
        {
            Debug.Log("[settings] reset to defaults");
        }

        public UniTask SaveAsync(CancellationToken ct)
        {
            // Pretends to write somewhere slow; unscaled, so a paused game still finishes.
            return UniTask.Delay(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1.5), DelayType.UnscaledDeltaTime, PlayerLoopTiming.Update, ct);
        }
    }
}
```

<!-- file: Samples~/ZenjectUsage/Support/ScoreService.cs -->

```csharp
namespace Ecanakli.UIDirector.Samples.ZenjectUsage
{
    /// <summary>Stand-in game state: a score the views read and change through the container.</summary>
    public sealed class ScoreService
    {
        public int Points { get; private set; }

        public void Add(int points)
        {
            Points += points;
        }

        public void Reset()
        {
            Points = 0;
        }
    }
}
```

<!-- file: CHANGELOG.md -->

# Changelog

All notable changes to this package are documented here. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the package uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-09

### Fixed

- **The integration menus now write their define to iOS and Windows Store Apps.** `Tools/UIDirector/Zenject Integration` and `Tools/UIDirector/DOTween Integration` skipped every build target whose value the `BuildTargetGroup` enum shares with an obsolete name (`iOS` with `iPhone`, `WSA` with `Metro`), so a build for those targets compiled without the integration. If you turned an integration on with 0.1.0, choose its menu item twice after updating (off, then on) so the define reaches every target, or add it to those targets in Player Settings.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-08

First release. Requires Unity 6000.0 or newer, UniTask and `com.unity.ugui`.

### Added

- **Root and layers.** `ViewRoot` sits on a canvas that the project owns and builds the layers, the input shield and the navigator under it. Three layers are built in: `screens` (a history stack that takes back), `popups` (modal, with a shared backdrop, closed by navigation) and `system` (modal blocking overlays). A project adds layers of its own with `ViewLayer` and `ViewLayerRules`. The menu `GameObject > UI > UIDirector Root` creates a root with a `BackInput` and an `EventSystem`; a camera variant creates a root with its own UI camera. `ViewRootSetup` initializes a root from code with an inject delegate, an asset provider, extra layers and an error handler. The root supports overlay and camera canvases, a persistent root across scenes, a numbered sorting band with a refusal instead of a wrap, a load indicator, load and transition timeouts, a waiting cap, `SafeAreaFitter` and the Prefab Mode UI environment.
- **Catalogs and keys.** `ViewCatalog` assets hold `ViewEntry` rows: an id, a prefab or an asset key, a layer, a retention, a back policy, a cover policy, a covered mode, close on backdrop and allow multiple. `ViewKey<TArgs, TResult>` names a row with its argument and result types, and a static class marked `[ViewKeys]` is checked against the catalogs by the editor. Catalogs are added to and removed from a running root through `INavigator.AddCatalog`, which takes an owner.
- **Opening and results.** `Open` returns a `ViewHandle` at once; `ShowAsync` completes with a `ViewResult<TResult>` in every case. A refusal, a failed load, a close by back or backdrop, an owner that ended and a destroyed root are data in the result (`CloseReason`, `RejectReason`, `HasValue`, `Value`), never exceptions. `OpenOptions` carries a source tag, `RejectWhenBusy` and a reserved request id. `ViewHandle.Close`, `WaitForCloseAsync`, `CloseAll` and the queries `IsOpen`, `TryGetOpen` and `TryGetTop` cover the rest of a view's life.
- **Owners.** Every open and every registration (`HoldInput`, `AddObserver`, `AddCatalog`, `PreloadAsync`) takes a required `CancellationToken` as its owner. When it ends, the view or registration ends. `INavigator.RootToken` is the explicit "as long as the UI exists" owner.
- **Navigation and back.** Screens stack on a history layer; opening an id that is already in the stack returns to it, and `CloseTo` pops everything above a screen. `Back()` is the single back rule and returns `false` when nothing handled the press. `BackPolicy` sets per row what back does, including `HandledByView`, which asks the view. `BackInput` turns the Escape key into `Back()` and raises `Unhandled`; with the Input System it reads Escape on any keyboard through an input action it owns, and it does nothing until its root is initialised. `ViewButton` gives buttons the actions Back, CloseView and OpenView without code.
- **Popups, overlays and input.** A shared backdrop under the top modal view, optional close on a backdrop tap, and an input shield that is counted and goes up in the same call that accepts a request. While it is up, back closes nothing but still withdraws the newest request that is waiting or loading. `HoldInput` blocks input from code. System overlays block input while they run. To hide the whole UI for a moment, the documentation gives a recipe: a `CanvasGroup` on the root with alpha 0 and `interactable` off, plus `HoldInput`.
- **View authoring.** `ViewBehaviour`, `ViewBehaviour<TArgs>` and `ViewBehaviour<TArgs, TResult>` are optional sugar over `IView<TArgs, TResult>`, `IViewVisible` and `IViewBack`. A view receives hooks that only begin things. Work that has to end is registered on a `ViewScope` (an open scope, and a visible scope for each span on screen) that the package ends on every path: `Bind` for a `UnityEvent`, `Subscribe` for any other event, `Add` for a disposable, `OnEnd` and `Run`. A view can `Decline` an open and `Complete` with a result. A catalog row can keep one idle instance per id, released by `Trim` and on `Application.lowMemory`.
- **Transitions.** `FadeTransition`, `ScaleTransition` and `SlideTransition` run on unscaled time, with a transition timeout and a synchronous `Snap`. One frame advances a built-in transition by at most 1/30 s, so below 30 fps it takes longer than its duration. `ViewTransition` is the base for transitions of your own and its contract is documented.
- **Queue.** `ViewQueue` presents requests one at a time by priority on one layer, above the navigator and through `INavigator` only. The constructor throws `ArgumentException` for a layer the root's navigator does not have. `IViewGate` allows or denies an item at enqueue and before presentation. Holds pause the queue, are counted and record the member and line that took them. Owners end waiting items. The queue hands the navigator one request at a time, so the navigator's waiting cap is never reached, and `EnqueueAsync` completes with the outcome also when an item never shows, including when the presentation itself fails. A queue ends when its lifetime ends or when its navigator's root is destroyed: waiting items end as not shown with `RejectReason.Cancelled` or `RejectReason.RootGone`, later calls are inert, and neither token keeps the queue alive. An item whose catalog row is on another layer than the queue's ends as not shown with `RejectReason.WrongLayer`. A feature can add its own catalog at run time with an owner.
- **Events and diagnostics.** `IViewObserver` receives `Enqueued`, `Requested`, `Shown`, `Closed`, `NotShown` and `Settled` events, in a documented order and without view arguments. `ViewErrorHandler` receives exceptions thrown by your own code. Problems carry stable ids `UIDIRECTOR101` to `UIDIRECTOR126`, each with a section in the Troubleshooting page: 101 to 120 and 126 at run time in the editor and development builds, 121 to 124 from the catalog validator, and 125 (a row with an empty id) from the validator and at run time when a catalog is registered. A view lost outside the package (destroyed or deactivated by other code) ends its request with `UIDIRECTOR107`; a kept instance lost that way is released, and the next open creates a new one. A text read-out is available through `INavigator.Describe`.
- **Editor tools.** `Window > UIDirector` shows the layers, requests, phases, shield holders and newest events live in Play Mode. `Tools/UIDirector/Validate Catalogs` checks every catalog in the project, from the menu, the catalog's Inspector and a batch entry point for a build pipeline. `Tools/UIDirector/Documentation` opens the documentation of the installed version, and the window and the catalog Inspector link each diagnostic to its Troubleshooting section.
- **Threading and cost.** Opening, registering and queueing throw on another thread; `ViewRegistration.Remove`, `CloseAll`, `Trim` and `ViewQueue.Clear` are posted to the main thread. An idle root, the queries, event dispatch and a running fade allocate nothing.
- **Addressables integration.** `AddressablesViewProvider` loads views by asset key and compiles when `com.unity.addressables` is installed. It supports preload leases through `PreloadAsync`, keeping and trimming, and the root's load timeout; the catalog validator warns about asset keys that match no address ([UIDIRECTOR124](Documentation~/Troubleshooting.md#uidirector124)).
- **DOTween integration.** `TweenTransition` is a transition configured in the Inspector, with a documented kill-safe pattern and a sample transition (`PunchTransition`) for writing your own on DOTween. It compiles when DOTween is present, and the menu `Tools/UIDirector/DOTween Integration` turns it on when only the DOTween assembly is in the project.
- **Zenject integration.** `NavigatorInstaller` binds the navigator and the root in a container, and the container injects every view instance the root creates. It compiles for Extenject 9.0.0 or newer as a package, and for Zenject under `Assets/` after `Tools/UIDirector/Zenject Integration`.
- **Samples.** Basic Usage, Queue Usage, Addressables Usage, DOTween Usage and Zenject Usage, each with a README, a scene and prefabs.
- **Documentation.** A README with a five-minute start, one guide per task, an API reference, a Troubleshooting page with one section per diagnostic id, design notes with five decision records, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for AI tools.
